annotation_description: Playing Mountain instead of Inspiring Vantage as the 3rd land. Inspiring Vantage enters untapped with 2 or fewer other lands (currently has 2), but next turn as the 4th land it will enter tapped. Mountain always enters untapped. By playing Mountain now and Inspiring Vantage next turn, the Inspiring Vantage will enter tapped, losing a mana on turn 4.

Played Sacred Foundry untapped (paying 2 life) before casting Slickshot Show-Off. The correct sequencing is to cast Slickshot Show-Off first using the 2 untapped Mountains ({1}{R}), then play Sacred Foundry tapped for free, saving 2 life unnecessarily spent.

At 5 life facing an evasive Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying) that can't be blocked by ground creatures, KimiK2 played Charming Prince instead of killing the Slickshot with Burst Lightning. Burst Lightning costs just {R} to deal 2 damage to the 1/2 Slickshot, killing it, and then there's still mana left to cast Charming Prince for the life gain. This leaves the flying threat alive that could easily deal lethal with any pump spell.

Targeting the opponent's face with Burst Lightning instead of Momo allows the opponent to block Slickshot Show-Off with Momo and survive at 3 life. Targeting Momo directly would kill Momo, guarantee Slickshot connects unblocked for 3 flying damage, and leave the opponent at 2 life instead of 3.

KimiK2 Stoic is at 1 life facing a 3/2 Slickshot Show-Off attack. They have Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant (which should be at least 2/2 or 3/3), Momo, Friendly Flier, and Charming Prince available as blockers. Any of these creatures could block the Slickshot Show-Off and prevent the lethal damage. The player's reasoning even correctly identifies they should block with Sarkhan, but somehow no blocker was actually assigned, resulting in the Slickshot dealing 3 damage and killing them.
